title: Map DPMI linear allocations lazily in the Unicorn host
description: The W2-048 replay establishes sparse host backing for DPMI AX=0501, but tools/probes/unicorn_int21.py still maps and zero-writes every byte of each successful allocation into Unicorn immediately. Implement page-on-first-access mapping for guest DPMI allocation ranges. Initialize each newly mapped page from GuestAddressSpace, mirror guest writes back, and make backing checks cover only materialized pages. Keep non-allocation invalid accesses as explicit stops and preserve the same DPMI addresses, handles, zero-fill, and errors.
acceptance: A guest DPMI allocation creates only a logical host range and does not eagerly mem_map or zero-write the whole block
First valid read/write in an allocated range maps only the touched pages and reads zero or prior host-backed bytes
Writes through Unicorn update GuestAddressSpace and survive a later access after page mapping
Invalid reads/writes outside all allocated ranges remain explicit unsupported-memory evidence
Original-byte -k replay preserves INT 2Fh AX=1500 and AX=0501 results, passes at least one million instructions, and records bounded materialized page count
Runtime and native guest-image regression suites pass
